hypothesis: Adopt the shadcn Dynamic Search contract as P05's agent-facing query API verbatim
rationale: shadcn already specifies GET /r/registry.json?q&type&limit&offset with a `pagination` object as the opt-in server-side-search signal, backwards compatible with static registries. Any shadcn-MCP-capable agent can then query Actionist with zero bespoke client work.
falsifier: If the contract cannot express the facets P05 needs (visual similarity, theme-eligibility, archetype role) even as extensions, and agents ignore unknown params, then a bespoke API is required after all.

hypothesis: Adopt canonical-component + alias-set, NOT a flat tag vocabulary
rationale: Component Gallery catalogues 60 canonical components each with an alias list, and its data empirically breaks flat naming: Banner is an alias of BOTH Alert and Hero; Stepper is both an alias of Progress indicator AND its own canonical; Label is an alias of Badge AND standalone. Our own 75-tag vocabulary averages 2.09 tags/component with 52.6% single-tagged, so it already behaves as a single-label category scheme, not a facet grid.
falsifier: If a sample of 200 components can be assigned to a 60-name canonical set by two independent raters with <80% agreement, the canonical model is not stable enough and faceted tags win.

hypothesis: Separate the index into two tiers by tag provenance and never let weak tags gate client-facing selection
rationale: Ground-truth `page` tags cover 4,033 components; `api` and `local` inference cover the rest. Measured per-shape, the gap is large: sidebar is 44 at page tier vs 139 at any tier. Presenting inferred tags as fact would mis-sell supply by up to 3x.
falsifier: If blind human review of 100 `local`-tier tag assignments finds >90% correct, the tier distinction is over-cautious and one merged index suffices.

hypothesis: Measure the visual near-duplicate rate with perceptual hash + CLIP before designing dedupe
rationale: Exact byte-identical previews are only 102 surplus of 7,678 (1.3%), while name-collision surplus is 2,058 (25.9%). The truth is between and is currently UNMEASURED; the gap is too large to design against.
falsifier: If pHash at a standard threshold collapses the 2,058 to under ~200 clusters, cheap hashing suffices and CLIP is unnecessary spend.

hypothesis: Actionist must OWN the archetype shell and the 20 AutoSaaS app primitives; harvest only decorative/marketing surfaces
rationale: Every AutoSaaS-required primitive has ground-truth supply in the corpus (min 32 for onboarding, max 167 for spinner), but these are exactly the components that must be contract-stable, themeable, accessible and wired to the data plane. Harvested bundles carry no source, no a11y contract and no props. Supply is not the constraint; ownership of the contract is.
falsifier: If a harvested table/form can be wired to P09's data plane and pass a11y checks in under a day each for 5 sampled components, owning them is wasted effort.

hypothesis: Treat the corpus as a dated snapshot, not a living layer, until a timestamp field exists
rationale: No meta.json in 7,949 dirs carries a harvest timestamp (fields are url/author/slug/name/description/installCommand/id/bundleUrl/previewUrl/harvested plus optional usage_count/demo_id/video_url/preview/previewVia). Directory mtimes cluster in a single 67-minute window on 2026-08-18. Staleness is currently uncomputable.
falsifier: If 21st.dev exposes a reliable per-component updated_at we can read at query time, a local timestamp is redundant.

hypothesis: Use the existing discovery frontier (urls-union) as the refresh queue; the design is mechanism-ready but legally gated
rationale: urls-union.union holds 8,225 discovered URLs against 7,949 harvested — a standing backlog of 276 already-discovered, unharvested components, and 0 harvested items missing from the union. The delta IS the refresh queue. But the mechanism that produced it is the one 21st.dev's terms prohibit.
falsifier: If counsel clears the harvest mechanism, this becomes a build task; if counsel refuses, the entire refresh design must move to licensed/first-party sources and this ranks last, not seventh.

hypothesis: Let clients select by visual attribute (colour, density, style), never by component name
rationale: Awwwards ships hex-swatch and font filtering; UIverse ships style tag facets (#neumorphism, #3d, #gradient); Mobbin ships Text-in-Screenshots so a user who cannot name a component can still search words printed on it. Our legacy store already carries visual_style across 24 values (minimalist 1739, flat 1315, gradient 768).
falsifier: If usability testing shows clients pick faster from a named-category list than from a visual grid, the visual-first premise is wrong.

hypothesis: Run the theme-eligibility gate over all 7,949 and publish pass/fail as a first-class index field
rationale: The prior audit proved a 12-token regex swap re-themes a bundle with JS bit-identical, and measured 55/60 (91.7%) re-theming cleanly, 86.7% of colour rules already tokenised, WebGL ~16% of n=25 and Tailwind-v3 8.3% of n=60 needing exclusion. Running it corpus-wide converts sampled estimates into a per-component fact and auto-produces the exclusion list.
falsifier: If the corpus-wide pass rate lands below ~60%, the re-theming premise fails and the picker must ship fixed-palette components instead.

hypothesis: Do NOT build an industry facet from legacy best_for_industries — it does not discriminate
rationale: Mean 3.93 industries per component; 171 components claim all 10; 89.6% claim saas. Worse, only 2 of the 17 target industries (real_estate, saas) have any direct analogue, and 5 (construction, logistics_freight, insurance_agencies, mortgage_brokers, property_management) have ZERO reachable supply under a best-effort crosswalk.
falsifier: If re-classifying a 200-component sample directly against the 17-industry list yields a balanced distribution, the axis is recoverable by reclassification rather than abandonment.

hypothesis: Perceptual hash (pHash/dHash/wHash) as the first dedupe pass
rationale: Cheap, well-understood, and idealo/imagededup bundles an evaluation harness.
falsifier: pHash fails to cluster components that differ only in theme colour.

hypothesis: CLIP embeddings as the second dedupe pass for semantic near-duplicates
rationale: Ports like shadcn-vue and shadcn-svelte guarantee semantically identical, pixel-different components.
falsifier: CLIP clusters by dominant colour rather than structure, producing useless clusters.

hypothesis: Cluster on the DOM/CSS structure of bundle.html rather than the image
rationale: Structure survives re-theming; pixels do not.
falsifier: Minified compiled bundles differ enough per build that structural hashes never collide.

hypothesis: One-per-author cap within a category to break house-style clustering
rationale: Top-10 authors hold 24.4% and top-50 hold 57.3% of the corpus; ruixen.ui alone has 383.
falsifier: Capping removes the best component in a category when one author is genuinely dominant.

hypothesis: Exclude junk/test fixtures by rule at index time
rationale: A corrected rule set flags 78 of 7,949 (0.98%): bare-test-name 15, localhost-author 38, fixture-string 21, numeric-name 14, char-repeat 11.
falsifier: The rules also catch legitimate components with terse names, harming recall.

hypothesis: Filter the client-facing picker to tagged components only
rationale: 670 untagged (8.4%) are largely junk by inspection; excluding them costs nothing a client would pick.
falsifier: Manual review of the 670 finds a materially useful minority.

hypothesis: Use usage_count as a popularity prior where present
rationale: usage_count is present on 1,125 of 3,000 sampled meta.json (37.5%).
falsifier: usage_count reflects 21st.dev install traffic, not fitness for our archetypes.

hypothesis: Rank by tag confidence first, damped by tag spread, installs as tiebreak
rationale: find.mjs already implements exactly this ranker.
falsifier: The ranker was tuned for a 832-entry catalog and does not generalise to 7,949.

hypothesis: Serve preview.webp in the grid and the bundle only on demand
rationale: Median preview 11,410 B vs median bundle 337,515 B — a ~30x scroll-performance difference.
falsifier: Static thumbnails cannot convey interaction, which is what differentiates many components.

hypothesis: Hover-to-play video preview for components with video_url
rationale: video_url is present on the same 1,125 of 3,000 sampled records as usage_count; board.html already implements hover-video.
falsifier: Only ~37% coverage makes the affordance inconsistent and confusing.

hypothesis: Virtualised grid; never pre-render cards
rationale: board.html is 885,238 B of pre-rendered HTML for only 832 cards (10.5% of corpus); that strategy cannot reach 7,949.
falsifier: A virtualised grid harms SEO/shareability that a static export would provide.

hypothesis: Progressive disclosure: pick 1 of ~10 per category, not browse 7,949
rationale: Supply per required shape is ample (ground truth 32-167), so the task is choosing 10, not finding any.
falsifier: Clients want to see the full range and feel constrained by a curated 10.

hypothesis: Side-by-side comparison of 2-3 candidates under the client's own token pack
rationale: Choice quality improves when alternatives are seen together under real theme.
falsifier: Comparison increases decision time without improving satisfaction.

hypothesis: Show each component in the client's palette BEFORE selection, not after
rationale: Closes the deterministic loop; the token swap is already proven mechanical.
falsifier: Re-theming introduces contrast failures that make good components look bad.

hypothesis: Scope token replacement to :root and .dark separately, never globally
rationale: 99.0% of bundles carry a .dark/prefers-color-scheme block; the prior proof rewrote every matching declaration including inside .dark, which collapses the dark variant.
falsifier: Clients only ever need one mode, making scoping unnecessary complexity.

hypothesis: Map white/N and black/N literals to color-mix() against theme tokens
rationale: A finite enumerable vocabulary of 39 distinct literal classes was observed across n=25; transparent/text-transparent are false positives needing no mapping.
falsifier: color-mix() browser support or visual result is unacceptable in target browsers.

hypothesis: Leave red/green/amber/yellow alone as semantic status colours
rationale: preetsuthar17__alert uses dark:bg-amber-950/30, dark:bg-blue-950/30, dark:bg-green-950/30 as warning/info/success variants; recolouring them to var(--primary) would make all three identical.
falsifier: Clients expect total palette control and find unrecoloured status chips inconsistent.

hypothesis: Exclude WebGL/shader components from theming and present them as fixed-palette effects
rationale: 4/25 sampled bundles carry ~130 vec3/vec4 colour constructions in GLSL strings that no CSS variable reaches; aurora-blur re-themed is a different component.
falsifier: A shader uniform can be driven from a CSS variable at runtime, making exclusion unnecessary.

hypothesis: Detect and route Tailwind v3 builds to a second mapping table
rationale: 5/60 bundles lack a shadcn token block; two are v3 builds using the --tw-bg-opacity idiom — equally enumerable, just different.
falsifier: The v3 population is too small and heterogeneous to justify a second mapper.

hypothesis: Make the eligibility gate a checkable per-component contract, not a corpus-wide assumption
rationale: Scanning post-swap CSS for any colour declaration not resolving through var()/color-mix(), ignoring transparent/currentColor, is ~20 lines and makes the guarantee per-component.
falsifier: The scan produces false failures on legitimate patterns, excluding good components.

hypothesis: Screenshot re-themed bundles headlessly and diff against the original to catch contrast failures
rationale: The audit flags 'do re-themed bundles look right' as the most likely source of unpleasant surprises and explicitly UNMEASURED.
falsifier: Automated contrast checks disagree with human aesthetic judgement often enough to be useless.

hypothesis: Compute WCAG contrast ratios post-theme and fail components below AA
rationale: Mechanical, cheap, and catches the light-first-component-on-dark-pack case.
falsifier: Many aesthetically fine components fail AA, making the gate too aggressive.

hypothesis: Join the two 21st stores on a NORMALISED canonical key, not raw URL string equality
rationale: The two stores use different URL shapes: meta.json.url is https://21st.dev/@author/components/slug while _provenance.fetchedFrom is https://21st.dev/r/Author/slug. Case-insensitive author+slug normalisation yields intersection 2,945, union 8,483.
falsifier: Author renames upstream break the key, silently splitting identities.

hypothesis: Carry source_available as a first-class index field
rationale: Only the legacy store has source: 3,506 components with real .tsx. Source-bearing supply is ~2.3x smaller than the 7,949 headline.
falsifier: Source becomes universally available via a paid key, making the field constant.

hypothesis: Prefer the legacy store's registry-item.json as the dependency record
rationale: It yields 237 distinct npm dependencies across the source-bearing store (lucide-react 1272, class-variance-authority 1031, framer-motion 874, @radix-ui/react-slot 824) — a real measurement, unlike the 18 packages visible from import-wrapper demo.tsx.
falsifier: Declared dependencies drift from what the source actually imports.

hypothesis: Use the legacy classification.json as the semantic/use-case axis
rationale: 3,507 of 3,507 carry use_cases (mean 4.63 each, 16,241 total) and 3,499 carry industries — the only local source of a job-to-be-done axis.
falsifier: Haiku-generated use_cases are too generic to discriminate between components.

hypothesis: Do NOT delete either 21st store as a duplicate
rationale: The 2,945 intersection holds source AND bundle AND preview; 534 legacy-only are source-bearing and absent from the newer corpus. Deleting either side destroys capability.
falsifier: Storage cost outweighs the value of the 534 legacy-only components.

hypothesis: Record every component with a provenance tier and refuse admission without one
rationale: Rights coverage is 2 license fields across 11,549 third-party records (0.017%).
falsifier: Counsel clears the corpus wholesale, making per-record provenance unnecessary.

hypothesis: Default every third-party record to rights_status: gated, reuse: reference_only
rationale: SISO harvest rule 6 says summarize rather than copy when licence is unclear; the corpus's own AGENT.md independently says adapt rather than paste.
falsifier: Counsel establishes blanket clearance.

hypothesis: Model the corpus as reference-for-regeneration, not a parts bin to copy
rationale: Sidesteps the rights problem: an agent that reads a bundle to learn a pattern and writes original source is doing what AGENT.md already instructs.
falsifier: Regenerated components are materially worse than the originals, negating the corpus's value.

hypothesis: Build the index so the corpus can be swapped for a licensed source without redesign
rationale: If counsel blocks 21st material, the index schema should survive with different rows.
falsifier: Source-specific fields leak into the schema deeply enough that swapping is a rewrite.

hypothesis: Treat registry.json-serving vendors as the licensed refresh path
rationale: ReactBits 672, Tailark 469, Aceternity 278, Magic UI 247, Fancy 158, HextaUI 139, Eldora 115, Kokonut 51, shadcn core 63 — all parsed live, all publishing a machine-readable registry by design rather than by scraping.
falsifier: Their individual licences prohibit redistribution as thoroughly as 21st's terms do.

hypothesis: Poll registry.json endpoints and diff item lists to detect new releases
rationale: Registries publish a full item list; a diff is the cheapest possible change feed.
falsifier: Registries do not version or timestamp items, so a diff cannot distinguish new from renamed.

hypothesis: Copy registry.directory's freshness telemetry model
rationale: It renders per-registry new-component deltas and updated-recency spanning same-day to 10 months — exactly the staleness signal P05 lacks.
falsifier: Its telemetry is manually curated rather than computed, and does not scale.

hypothesis: Show clients a per-component last-verified date
rationale: Trust in a 'living' layer depends on visible recency.
falsifier: Clients ignore dates and it only exposes staleness we would rather fix.

hypothesis: Re-capture previews on a change-detection trigger, not a fixed schedule
rationale: changedetection.io (Apache-2.0) implements exactly this; fixed schedules waste quota on unchanged components.
falsifier: Change detection over rendered pages is too noisy to be a useful trigger.

hypothesis: Backfill the 271 missing previews with Playwright rather than the vendor CDN
rationale: backfill-previews.mjs exists but was never run; Playwright renders from the local bundle with no vendor request.
falsifier: Local renders differ visually from vendor previews, making the grid inconsistent.

hypothesis: Close the 276-component discovery backlog before any new discovery sweep
rationale: Cheapest possible corpus growth: they are already discovered and unharvested.
falsifier: The 276 are non-components or dead URLs.

hypothesis: Keep serve.mjs and find.mjs; rebuild the data layer only
rationale: serve.mjs already serves harvest/ correctly and implements the POST /api/picks manifest contract end to end; find.mjs implements ranking and a --json agent surface.
falsifier: Their assumptions are tied to the 832-entry catalog and do not survive contact with 7,949.

hypothesis: Steal board.html's CSS and interaction model, discard its markup and data
rationale: It has a responsive auto-fill grid, lazy loading, light/dark tokens, multi-select with a sticky tray, lightbox and hover-video — but is a static snapshot of 832 of 7,949 (10.5%) pointing at a different preview store.
falsifier: The CSS is entangled with the pre-rendered markup and cannot be lifted cleanly.

hypothesis: Generate one slim picker-index.json rather than shipping three 700KB+ JSON files
rationale: classification.json is 2.17 MB, api-metadata.json 1.30 MB, catalog.json 713 KB, ranked.json 844 KB.
falsifier: A single index becomes a bottleneck for partial updates.

hypothesis: Adopt the Great Library 11-stage lifecycle rather than inventing an admission ladder
rationale: It already encodes unverified -> read -> candidate -> ... -> retired with evidence[] and blockers[] requirements.
falsifier: The lifecycle is tuned for repos, not components, and the stages do not map.

hypothesis: Schematize KEEPERS.md into structured records
rationale: It is the only local artifact encoding human component admission, and it is prose.
falsifier: It is too small a precedent to be worth schematizing.

hypothesis: Own navigation as an archetype-level structure, not a harvested component
rationale: Navigation encodes route topology and permission state from P10, which no harvested component can know.
falsifier: A harvested nav shell can be parameterised by a route manifest without modification.

hypothesis: Own forms because validation, error state and submission are contract surfaces
rationale: Form field supply exists (120 ground truth) but a harvested field has no schema, no validation contract and no data-plane binding.
falsifier: A generated schema-to-form layer can wrap harvested field visuals without owning them.

hypothesis: Own tables because sorting, pagination, selection and empty/loading/error states are behavioural
rationale: 141 ground-truth table components exist, but the behaviour matters more than the look.
falsifier: A headless table library plus harvested styling covers it without ownership.

hypothesis: Own the feedback family (toast, alert, empty, loading, error) as one coherent set
rationale: These must be consistent across an app; sourcing them from five different authors guarantees incoherence.
falsifier: Theme tokens alone are enough to make five authors' feedback components look coherent.

hypothesis: Harvest heroes, testimonials, pricing sections, galleries and marketing surfaces
rationale: These are decorative, self-contained, carry no data-plane contract, and are exactly where visual variety has client value. hero=521, testimonials=137, pricing-section=186, gallery=325.
falsifier: Marketing surfaces still need CMS binding, making them contract-bearing after all.

hypothesis: Define an owned base set of roughly 20 components matching the AutoSaaS requirement list
rationale: AutoSaaS already enumerates 20 required primitives with a metadata contract (name, use case, props, states, a11y notes, responsive behavior, source path, examples, tests).
falsifier: The 20 are wrong for Actionist's archetypes and a different set is needed.

hypothesis: Derive the owned set from archetype demand, not from a generic dashboard list
rationale: case_workflow is primary for 6 of 17 industries and portal secondary for 6 of 17; two archetypes carry majority demand.
falsifier: Archetype-level reuse is an illusion and per-industry sets are required.

hypothesis: Version owned components independently with their own contracts
rationale: teambit/bit demonstrates component-as-independently-versioned-unit at scale.
falsifier: Independent versioning overhead exceeds its benefit at ~20 components.

hypothesis: Express owned components as a shadcn-compatible registry Actionist publishes
rationale: Makes Actionist's own base layer consumable by any shadcn-aware agent or client.
falsifier: Publishing invites support obligations Actionist does not want.

hypothesis: Give every component an a11y contract field with observed evidence, not a claim
rationale: Component Gallery carries 'Accessibility issues (4)' and 'Accessibility guidelines (27)' as first-class facets on design systems.
falsifier: Automated a11y checks on isolated components produce too many false positives.

hypothesis: Carry 'unmaintained' and 'has known issues' as first-class facets
rationale: Component Gallery does exactly this for design systems (Unmaintained 11 of 95).
falsifier: For a component corpus these facets are unknowable without upstream signals.

hypothesis: Store components in an embedded vector store colocated with metadata
rationale: pgvector or lancedb avoids a second datastore while enabling similarity + facet filtering in one query.
falsifier: Metadata filtering plus vector search in one engine is slower than two specialised ones.

hypothesis: Expose an MCP server over the component index
rationale: Mobbin and 21st.dev both ship one; it is the emerging norm for agent access.
falsifier: MCP adoption stalls and a plain HTTP API would have served better.

hypothesis: Return accessibility-tree summaries rather than images to agents where possible
rationale: playwright-mcp uses accessibility-tree-over-pixels; Mobbin's own guidance caps at 3-8 images per call because each consumes context.
falsifier: Agents select components better from images than from structural text.

hypothesis: Cap agent responses at a small number of candidates with structured metadata
rationale: Mobbin enforces a default limit of 20 screens per call at 60 req/min.
falsifier: Agents need broad candidate sets and small caps degrade selection quality.

hypothesis: Publish an llms.txt describing the corpus and its query surface
rationale: Verified present on 21st.dev, Magic UI, Aceternity, Creative Tim, daisyUI and others; cheap static discoverability.
falsifier: llms.txt is ignored by the agents that matter.

hypothesis: Let agents query by archetype role rather than by component name
rationale: An agent composing a case_workflow app needs 'the table for this archetype', not 'table'.
falsifier: Archetype role is too coarse and agents still need name-level control.

hypothesis: Return a re-themed preview URL in agent responses so the agent can verify visually
rationale: Closes the loop between selection and appearance.
falsifier: Agents cannot meaningfully evaluate a rendered preview and the extra payload is waste.

hypothesis: Expose the theme-eligibility flag in the agent query so ineligible components are never returned
rationale: Prevents an agent selecting a component that will ignore the client's palette.
falsifier: Eligibility is contextual and a global flag over-excludes.

hypothesis: Support text-in-preview search via OCR over the 7,678 previews
rationale: Mobbin ships Text-in-Screenshots as a distinct search dimension; it needs no taxonomy at all.
falsifier: Component previews contain mostly lorem ipsum, so OCR adds no signal.

hypothesis: Extract a dominant-colour palette per preview and allow colour-swatch filtering
rationale: Awwwards ships hex-swatch filtering as a verified non-technical browse affordance.
falsifier: Components are re-themed anyway, so their captured colour is irrelevant to choice.

hypothesis: Filter by visual density/complexity using the legacy complexity axis
rationale: complexity is populated across the source store: composite 2201, atomic 1261, system 44.
falsifier: Complexity as labelled does not correlate with what clients perceive as busy.

hypothesis: Filter by visual_style using the legacy 24-value axis
rationale: minimalist 1739, flat 1315, gradient 768, dark 274, glass-morphism 260, 3d 248 — a real, populated style axis.
falsifier: Style labels are Haiku-generated and do not match human judgement.

hypothesis: Show interaction affordances as a facet
rationale: The legacy store carries an interactions axis (hover-glow, morph, scroll-animate observed).
falsifier: Coverage of the interactions field is too sparse to filter on.

hypothesis: Let clients pick by reference image: upload a screenshot, retrieve visually similar components
rationale: CLIP embeddings make image-to-image retrieval straightforward.
falsifier: Clients do not have reference images, or the matches are too loose to be useful.

hypothesis: Let clients pick by describing the job in plain words, matched against use_cases
rationale: 16,241 use_case strings exist across 3,507 components, averaging 4.63 each.
falsifier: Use-case text is too generic to discriminate between similar components.

hypothesis: Present a small curated shelf per archetype rather than the whole corpus
rationale: The binding constraint is curation, not supply.
falsifier: Clients reject curated shelves as limiting and demand full browse.

hypothesis: Record every client selection as training signal for P06
rationale: Selections are the highest-quality preference data available.
falsifier: Selection is dominated by position and ordering effects rather than preference.

hypothesis: Track which curated candidates are never chosen and retire them
rationale: Cheap corpus quality signal.
falsifier: Non-selection reflects ordering, not quality.

hypothesis: A/B the curated top-10 per category against random draws from the eligible set
rationale: Directly tests whether curation adds value.
falsifier: Client volume is too low for statistical power.

hypothesis: Measure time-to-first-selection as the primary UX metric
rationale: Operationalises 'a client can choose without knowing component names'.
falsifier: Fast selection correlates with disengagement rather than confidence.

hypothesis: Let clients reject a whole visual style in one action to prune the space fast
rationale: Negative preference is faster to elicit than positive.
falsifier: Style rejection removes components clients would have liked individually.

hypothesis: Keep a human greenlight gate for anything client-facing
rationale: KEEPERS.md is the only local precedent for admission and it is human-greenlit.
falsifier: Human review cannot keep pace and becomes the bottleneck.

hypothesis: Score components on completeness and flag partial ones
rationale: ranked.json already carries completeness and flags fields.
falsifier: Those scores were computed for 832 entries and do not generalise.

hypothesis: Deprioritise components whose previews are under 2KB unless they are known primitives
rationale: Under-2KB is 6.1% of a 196-preview sample and correlates with small primitives rather than corruption.
falsifier: Small previews are legitimate and deprioritising them loses good primitives.

hypothesis: Treat the 121 bundle-less components as index-only records
rationale: verify-harvest.mjs reconciles 7,949 = 7,828 with a bundle + 121 without, and PASSes.
falsifier: They are recoverable and should simply be re-harvested.

hypothesis: Never present a component whose preview is missing
rationale: 271 of 7,949 lack preview.webp; a card with no image is worse than no card.
falsifier: A generated placeholder render is adequate.

hypothesis: Build the index incrementally so a partial refresh never invalidates the whole
rationale: A monolithic regenerate is what makes board.html unmaintainable.
falsifier: Incremental complexity is not worth it at this corpus size.

hypothesis: Store previews content-addressed to make dedupe and cache invalidation trivial
rationale: Hashing previews already revealed 65 exact-duplicate groups.
falsifier: Content addressing complicates the simple author__slug path convention.

hypothesis: Keep the 75-tag vocabulary as a retrieval index but not as the client-facing taxonomy
rationale: It is dense enough for search (mean 2.09 tags) but too flat and collision-prone to present.
falsifier: Clients navigate the 75 tags comfortably in testing.

hypothesis: Map the 75 tags onto a two-level hierarchy for browsing
rationale: Ant Design's General/Layout/Navigation/Data Entry/Data Display/Feedback is a proven top level.
falsifier: Any two-level mapping puts too many components under one node to be navigable.

hypothesis: Distinguish structural role from visual treatment as separate axes
rationale: headlessui's behaviour/appearance split is the canonical precedent, and conflating them is why 'hero' and 'background' both appear as tags.
falsifier: Clients think in conflated terms and separating the axes confuses them.

hypothesis: Add an explicit archetype-role axis absent from both stores
rationale: Neither store knows whether a table is a case list or an invoice ledger.
falsifier: Archetype role is a composition concern belonging to P12, not the component layer.

hypothesis: Reclassify a sample directly against the 17 industries to test recoverability
rationale: The existing industry axis is near-uniform and misses 5 of 17 entirely.
falsifier: Reclassification produces the same uniform distribution, proving components are genuinely industry-agnostic.

hypothesis: Accept that most UI components ARE industry-agnostic and drop industry from the component layer
rationale: 89.6% claim saas and 171 claim all 10 industries — the data may be telling the truth.
falsifier: Industry-specific component demand shows up clearly once archetype-level composition is modelled.

hypothesis: Carry framework/stack as a hard filter
rationale: 237 distinct npm dependencies were measured; three (lucide-react, class-variance-authority, framer-motion) dominate.
falsifier: Stack can be normalised at generation time, making it a soft preference.

hypothesis: Flag heavyweight dependencies (three, gsap, @react-three/fiber) at index time
rationale: three appears in 85 components, gsap 57, @react-three/fiber 29.
falsifier: Bundle-size impact is acceptable and the flag causes needless exclusion.

hypothesis: Use dependency overlap as a secondary near-duplicate signal
rationale: Components with identical dependency sets and similar names are strong duplicate candidates.
falsifier: Dependency sets are too uniform (lucide-react in 1,272) to discriminate.

hypothesis: Detect cross-framework ports as a distinct duplicate class
rationale: shadcn-vue and shadcn-svelte are literal ports of shadcn/ui.
falsifier: Our corpus is React-only, making the class empty.

hypothesis: Publish the corpus join as a reproducible script, not a one-off report
rationale: Counts drift; every number should be re-derivable on demand.
falsifier: The corpus is static enough that re-derivation is wasted effort.

hypothesis: Fail the build if index counts diverge from a fresh count of the stores
